design: MemoryContextAssembler implements the LLD 2.8.1 port (selection, redaction, ordering, truncation and influence receipt) over the closed MemoryContextAssemblyRequest/MemoryContextAssembly of reports/contracts/ocor-governed-memory.openapi.yaml; to_mapping returns exactly the ten contract fields.
Selection is the audited policy-first searchMemory of 0052 under the same governed context (a search under another GCS is refused before any search); the search receipt is pinned by search_audit_ref.

Every selected exact version is re-validated with the 0052 eligibility (exact committed head, ACTIVE, no deletion epoch, compartments, marking, live materialisation decision) before and after its content read and once more over all versions before the receipt; the stop epoch of the plan must hold after every read and before the receipt. A change fails closed (CANDIDATE_CHANGED / STOP_EPOCH_MISMATCH) and changed content never reaches the context policy.

A live MemoryContextPolicy decides inclusion per exact version and target model and returns ordered, non-overlapping redaction spans with closed reason codes; outages, invalid decisions and bundle mismatch fail closed. Excluded versions appear only in the audit receipt.

Rendering separates data from instructions: header line plus one RFC 8785 canonical JSON line per block with role UNTRUSTED_MEMORY_DATA, kind, scope, source, taint, instruction_eligible, marking, content digest and the escaped (redacted) data; payload text cannot add a line, member or role.
Ordering is the retrieval rank; truncation keeps the longest whole-block prefix within max_context_bytes and records the cut versions; a budget below the header fails closed.

The receipt binds query digest, representation versions, ranking profile digest, candidates with item/content digests, exclusions, blocks (position, spans, redaction refs, block digest/bytes, included), truncation record, rendering profile digest, context ref and SHA-256 context digest; live policy decision refs are recorded outside the replay-determining core. The receipt is written through the audit port before the context is returned (no audit, no context); every refusal after the envelope is an audited denial.

replay(audit_ref) reads the receipt from the audit store, verifies body and core digests, requires the same GCS, query digest, target model, budget and rendering profile, re-materialises the recorded versions in recorded order under live policy without re-ranking, and returns the context only when the recomputed core digest equals the recorded one.

normative_interpretations: FGM-20 exact replay is interpreted as re-materialisation of the recorded exact versions in recorded order with live re-validation, not as re-execution of ranking: recency factors depend on the evaluation clock, so re-ranking cannot be exact. A replay whose versions are no longer live-eligible (correction, revocation, reclassification, deletion, policy change) fails closed instead of reproducing content: most restrictive reading of ADD v1.3 Part II 2.10/2.12 (no resurrection, live policy at every use). Exact replay of superseded versions for audit purposes is therefore verified only through the receipt digests, without content.
Policy decision references are recorded beside the replay core, not inside it: a decision is re-evaluated live at replay and only its effect (inclusion and redaction spans) must be identical.
The response exposes only included versions; versions excluded by the context policy are recorded in the protected audit receipt only, so the response does not disclose them.

Backlog requirement BR-003 is the generic task requirement; following the sealed G5 practice the cases are bound to FR-118 (context-assembly tests of ADD v1.3 Part II section 3) and FR-119 (non-interference and kill-switch races) as component-level evidence only; G6 binding to requirements remains with 0060-0066.

requirement_coverage_note: Component-level evidence for the context-assembly obligation of FR-118 (MemoryContextAssembly receipt and exact replay, FGM-20 oracle) and the non-interference/kill-switch aspects of FR-119 at the context boundary, plus BR-003; no G6 verification, no FGM campaign closure, no E1/E2 or Verified promotion.

requirement_results.command: MemoryContextAssembly receipt (closed ten-field contract record) binds the query digest, the representation versions and ranking profile digest of the pinned search receipt, the exact selected versions with item and content digests in retrieval order, every redaction span and reason (never the removed text), the whole-block-prefix truncation record and the SHA-256 final context digest; rendering keeps memory as escaped UNTRUSTED_MEMORY_DATA blocks; on PostgreSQL 16, Qdrant and OpenBao for all four retrieval modes the receipt is durably appended and read back by audit_ref

FGM-20 oracle at component level: replay by audit_ref re-materialises the recorded versions in recorded order (no re-ranking, recency drift irrelevant) with the same redactions and truncation and yields byte-identical context and identical contract fields; on the real backends from fresh adapters and connections of a new run in every retrieval mode

Unknown, foreign, tampered or rewritten receipts and a different query, budget, target model or governed context are refused before any content read (RECEIPT_UNRECORDED / RECEIPT_DIGEST_MISMATCH / REPLAY_INPUT_UNRECORDED / REPLAY_CONTEXT_MISMATCH); correction, revocation, reclassification, materialisation denial, changed redaction or exclusion and a kill switch make replay fail closed (CANDIDATE_CHANGED / CONTEXT_REPLAY_MISMATCH / STOP_EPOCH_MISMATCH) with an audited denial and no context, also on the real backends

The closed MemoryContextAssemblyRequest, binding, GCS digest, deadline, budget, rendering profile and search-under-the-same-GCS are checked before any search; context policy outage, invalid decision, stale bundle and malformed redaction spans fail closed with an audited, digest-only denial; no audit means no context; content not binding its committed digest is never rendered

On the real backends, worlds with and without the twenty-one unauthorized or ineligible items of the 0052 corpus (foreign or mixed compartment, tenant, organization, marking, purpose, domain, project, run, agent, federation, quarantined, proposed, expired, not-yet-valid, elapsed validity, pending projection, revoked, policy-denied, other kind, reclassified) produce byte-identical contexts, selections and truncation records in all four modes; a kill switch or a revocation during assembly or during a content read leaves no context and no success receipt, and changed content never reaches the context policy

residual_risks: The receipt audit store of the qualifying cases is a test adapter on the real PostgreSQL; no production audit service with tamper-evident storage exists yet, so receipt authenticity rests on the digest self-binding plus the store boundary (open, unassigned).
The window between the final re-validation and the return of the context is not atomic with respect to a concurrent revocation (same limitation as 0052 search); no FGM-17 claim is made.
Redaction spans are produced by the context policy port; this task verifies their enforcement and recording, not the quality of any redaction classifier (no OPA context policy bundle exists yet).
Context digests and block digests in audit are non-content references that may be correlatable; the membership-inference risk declared in 0055 remains open and unassigned.
